lines.en: Good morning! **How can I help you?**
Hi! **I’d like to book** a trip to Chicago, please.
lines.pt: Oi! Eu gostaria de reservar uma viagem para Chicago, por favor.

lines.en: Sure. When do you want to go?

lines.pt: No dia 10 de junho. É direto?

lines.en: Yes, it’s a direct flight. It takes two hours.
lines.pt: Sim, é um voo direto. Leva duas horas.
Quanto custa uma passagem de ida e volta?

lines.en: It’s $180. You can pay a $30 deposit today.
lines.pt: Custa 180 dólares. Você pode pagar um sinal de 30 dólares hoje.

lines.en: Of course. Your full name, please?
lines.pt: Claro. Seu nome completo, por favor?

pages.title: Booking a trip

situation.text: You go to a travel office to book a trip. You choose the place and the date, ask if the flight is direct, ask the price and ask how to pay.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can book a simple trip: say where and when, ask if it is direct, ask the price and the way to pay.
canDo: Make the request: I’d like to book…
Ask: Is it direct? / How much is…?
Ask about payment: Can I pay by card?
success: I say where I want to go.
pages.think: When you book a trip, what do you want to know first: price, date or time? Is it the same in all countries?

teach.goal: Abrir pela situação real: reservar uma viagem. Foco em pedir, perguntar preço e confirmar.
solo: Pergunte como o aluno costuma reservar viagens (site, agência, app).
Mostre os 4 critérios de sucesso.
group: Cada aluno diz um lugar que quer visitar.
extra: Where do you want to go?
Do you book online or in an office?
support: Aceite respostas curtas (“Chicago.”) e devolva a frase completa.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — booking a trip
pages.intro: Today many people book trips online or by app, but travel offices still exist. Look at the cards and guess why each detail matters.

cards.note: A direct flight is faster; a flight with a stop can be cheaper.
Some bookings ask you to pay a small part now and the rest later.
After you book online, you usually get a confirmation by email. Keep it.

qs.q: Why is “Is it direct?” a useful question?
qs.pt: Por que “Is it direct?” é uma pergunta útil?

levels.A2: A direct trip has no stops.
levels.B1: It tells you if you need to change planes, which affects time and price.
levels.B2: It helps you compare total travel time and stress against the price of cheaper options.

levels.A2: A small part of the price that you pay now.
levels.B1: A first payment that keeps your reservation; you pay the rest later.
levels.B2: A partial payment that secures the booking, often with rules about refunds.

qs.q: What should you check before you pay?
qs.pt: O que você deve conferir antes de pagar?

levels.A2: The date, the name and the price.
levels.B1: The date, the name on the ticket and the total price.
levels.B2: Dates, spelling of your name, total cost and the cancellation rules.

pages.compare: In Brazil you also book online and by app, and sometimes pay in installments (parcelado). In many places in the USA, people pay for the whole trip at once or a deposit for hotels. What do you do where you live?

teach.goal: Mostrar três detalhes úteis na reserva: direto × escala, sinal (deposit) e confirmação por e-mail. Evite números ou regras específicas de empresas.
solo: Mostre os cartões e peça hipóteses.
Compare com o parcelamento no Brasil.
group: Cada aluno escolhe um cartão e explica.
answers: Q1: saber se tem escala; afeta tempo e preço.
Q3: data, nome e preço total.
extra: Do you read the confirmation email?
Is a cheaper ticket always better?
stretch: B2: o que fazer se o nome na passagem estiver errado?

patterns.name: Making a request
patterns.formula: **I’d like to book** + trip / room / ticket
ex: I’d like to book a trip to Chicago.
I’d like to book a room.
I’d like to book two tickets.

patterns.name: Asking the price
patterns.formula: **How much is** + noun? / **How much are** + nouns?

swap.frame: I’d like to book a {item} to {place} on {date}.
swap.tpt: Eu gostaria de reservar {item} para {place} em {date}.

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: I’d like to book a trip.
I would like to make a reservation for a trip.
Is payment by credit card accepted?
register.note: These are differences of context, not strict rules.

teach.goal: Fixar 2 padrões principais: I’d like to book… e How much is…?. A data (June 10) entra como bloco.
solo: Mostre os padrões no diálogo.
Use a troca de palavras com o destino do aluno.
group: Em pares: um escolhe as peças, o outro fala.
teach.answers: Padrões 01 e 02 são o foco; 03 é expansão.
extra: Change the place and the date.
Ask the price of two tickets.

support: Fique só com I’d like to book…

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — numbers and prices
pages.tip: Teens and tens sound similar: 13 /ˌθɜːrˈtiːn/ has the strong syllable at the end; 30 /ˈθɜːrti/ has it at the start. “One eighty” can mean $180.

own.prompt: Write a price for a ticket, like “It’s $__”. Say it with the right stress.
own.criteria: Say it twice. Does your partner hear 13 or 30?

solo: Bata palmas na sílaba forte.
Faça o aluno ditar preços e você escreve.
group: Cada aluno diz o próprio preço.
answers: Identify 1: It’s thirty dollars. · Identify 2: It’s fifteen dollars.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short email to a travel office to ask about a trip. Say where, when and ask the price.

pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea.

ladder.say: I’d like a ticket to Boston. How much?
ladder.goal: Ask for a ticket and the price.

ladder.say: I’d like to book a round-trip ticket to Boston on June 10. Is it direct?

ladder.say: Could you tell me if there are any cheaper flights that leave in the morning?
I’d prefer a flexible fare in case I need to change the date, even if it costs a bit more.
Given the tight schedule, I’d rather pay a premium for a direct flight than risk a missed connection.
If it’s all the same to you, I’ll hold off on the deposit until the itinerary is confirmed.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own.
